readme.summary: The README identifies the tool and lists supported architectures clearly, but defers almost all usage guidance to external documentation with no examples or quick-start content.
readme.top_issue: No quick-start example or usage demonstration — users are simply pointed to external docs with no inline guidance on how to assemble even a minimal file.

injection_risks.description: The _parse_and_add_definition function does not validate user input for potential injection risks, but it appears to be used only with internal data.
The print_text_using_args function uses vsnprintf which can lead to buffer overflows if the format string is not properly validated, but it appears to be used only with internal data.

critical_findings: Potential buffer overflow in print_text_using_args function
security.summary: The wla-dx assembler package has some potential security concerns, including lack of input validation and potential buffer overflows, but overall appears to be a relatively secure piece of software.

common_complaints: Assembler behavior inconsistencies (-h flag forcing wrong operand sizes, signed/unsigned literal handling)

Path resolution issues (-I flag ignored in certain contexts like .stringmaptable)

Namespace/label reference issues with isolated includes
